_what_this_is: Canonical copy of the hand-authored content in maps/san-diego-land-holders/index.html. These records are NOT derived from CPAD, SANDAG, Census TIGERweb or any other dataset in the build pipeline. If the page is regenerated and this content is dropped, it cannot be rebuilt from source data - restore it from here.
_why_it_exists: The parcel layer (DATA.cats) is fully reproducible from source datasets. PINS, DATA.ranchos and DATA.wild are not. They survived nine rebuild generations only because every rebuild script rewrote the single line beginning "const DATA = " and left the script body alone. That is a convention, not a safeguard.
_verifying: node maps/san-diego-land-holders/sources/verify.js compares the page against this file and exits non-zero if they diverge.
_cpad_probe_method: Each name was reduced to its distinctive tokens (words over 3 characters, excluding generic ones such as san, rancho, park, mission, wilderness) and tested against every UNIT_NAME, SITE_NAME, AGNCY_NAME and LABEL_NAME in the five cached CPAD pages. Matches were then read individually; cpad_name_probe records that reading, not the raw hit count.
_finding: None of the 65 entries can be reconstructed from CPAD. Five have a same-site CPAD polygon, but CPAD carries neither their historic designations, nor their marker coordinates, nor their descriptions.

pins.t: The 13,299-acre 1845 Mexican grant, later expanded to about 22,000–23,000 acres. Often called the last California rancho still intact within its original boundaries.
